gaps.sentence: This cup is cracked — could I have ___ one?
gaps.explanation: 'Another one' means one more, unspecified; 'the other one' would mean a specific second cup.

gaps.sentence: We need to find ___ who can fix the boiler.
gaps.hint: affirmative statement: an unknown but existing person
gaps.explanation: 'Someone' is used in affirmative sentences; 'anyone' belongs to questions and negatives.

gaps.sentence: ___ lakes in this region freeze in winter.
gaps.explanation: 'Most lakes' speaks about lakes in general; 'most of' would need 'the lakes'.

gaps.sentence: It's so quiet here — there's hardly ___ around.
gaps.explanation: 'Hardly' is a negative adverb, so it combines with 'anybody' (hardly anybody = almost nobody); 'nobody' would double the negative.

gaps.sentence: ___ the food was eaten within minutes.
gaps.explanation: 'All the food' is correct with an uncountable noun; 'whole' needs 'the whole of' and 'both' needs two separate items.

gaps.sentence: We see our grandparents ___ other weekend.
gaps.explanation: 'Every other weekend' means alternate weekends; 'each other' has a different, reciprocal meaning.
'Some' is used in offers and requests where we expect agreement; 'any' is for neutral questions.

gaps.sentence: ___ of the workforce is part-time now.
gaps.hint: pattern: ___ of + specific group; singular verb
gaps.explanation: 'Half of the workforce is ...' is the correct pattern; 'the half of' is not used in this position.
